julian_warden.text: In the 1370s a woman we call Julian of Norwich lived walled up in a little cell beside this church, an anchoress, praying and giving advice through a window.

She wrote Revelations of Divine Love: the earliest surviving book in English that we know was written by a woman. Her most famous line is: all shall be well, and all shall be well, and all manner of thing shall be well.
The church was bombed flat in 1942 and rebuilt after the war, round tower and all. Norfolk has more round-tower churches than anywhere else in England. Flint is hard to make corners from, you see.
